loginIntro: Platform operations. Sign in with an account that holds the admin role.
forbiddenBody: Your account is signed in, but it does not hold the admin role — so none of the screens here would load any data for you.
forbiddenFootnote: Admin access is granted by a platform operator, never through sign-up.
crashBody: Nothing was changed by this error — it happened while drawing the page, not while saving. Reload to try again. If it repeats, the details below identify the bug.
ofUnknownAttempts: of an unknown number of attempts
leadPipelineSub: Every lead on the platform, by status
recentSignupsSub: The newest accounts on the platform
noAccountsYetOverviewSub: Nobody has registered on this platform. The five newest accounts will appear here as soon as somebody does.
applicationsNoticeTitle: Approving promotes the account's role from Buyer to Agent.
applicationsNoticeBody: This is the only path to an agent account — a realtor status is an application, not a permission. Approving records the decision and cannot be silently undone; demoting the account later leaves their listings behind.
emptyQueueClearSub: No realtor application is waiting on a decision.
emptyApprovedSub: Nobody has been granted agent access through this queue yet.
emptyRejectedSub: No application has been turned down yet.
staleDecisionSuffix: ’s application was already decided by another admin, so nothing was changed. The queue has been refreshed.
couldNotRefreshList: Could not refresh the list: {{message}}. The rows below are from the last successful load.
noApplicationDetails: This account carries a realtor status but no application details — nothing was recorded when the status was set.
approveConsequenceSuffix: agent access to the platform. Their role changes from Buyer to Agent and they can publish listings immediately. This is the only path to an agent account, and it cannot be silently undone — demoting them later leaves their listings behind.
rejectConsequenceSuffix: ’s application. Their account stays a buyer, with no agent access and no way to publish. The decision is recorded against their profile and cannot be reversed from here.
usersDirectorySub: Role is what an account can do; realtor status is only what it applied for.
emptyNoMatchQuerySub: Nothing has “{{q}}” in its name or email under the current role and status filters.
emptyNoMatchSub: No account on the platform has this combination of role and realtor status.
emptyFreshDatabaseSub: Every registration lands in this list, so an empty one means a fresh database — check the environment strip above before reading anything else on this screen.
couldNotReadDirectory: Could not read the directory: {{message}}. The rows above are from the last successful load.
roleUnchangedWarning: That is the role this account already has. Pick a different one, or cancel.
adminGrantNoticeTitle: This is the strongest permission the platform has.
adminGrantNoticeBody: Every other role change on this screen is undone by making the opposite one. This one hands over the ability to make that reversal impossible.
roleConsequenceUnchanged: {{name}} already holds the {{role}} role. Choose a different role to make a change.
roleConsequenceAdminGrant: Admin is the widest role on the platform. {{name}} will be able to change anyone's role — including yours — approve or reject any realtor application, and read every account, ad and lead in the control room. Nothing here can take that back except another role change made from an admin session, and the server refuses even that once they are the only admin left. Grant this only to someone who already has that authority off-screen.
roleConsequenceAdminRevoke: {{name}} loses control-room access on their next request: no applications, no users, no audit log. The server refuses this if they are the last admin account, and refuses it outright if {{name}} is you.
roleConsequenceCoworker: {{name}} will act inside their owning agent's data instead of their own — the same leads and listings that agent sees. The server refuses this unless an agent has already invited the account, because a coworker with no agent behind it can reach the Work tab and see nothing.
roleConsequenceAgent: {{name}} will be able to post listings and work leads under their own name. Their realtor application is left exactly as it stands — approving an application is the separate action on the Applications screen, and this does not stand in for it.
roleConsequenceBuyerOwned: {{name}} loses the Work tab. Nothing is deleted: the {{owned}} on this account stay exactly where they are, owned by someone who can no longer manage them.
roleConsequenceBuyer: {{name}} loses the Work tab and keeps only the buyer side of the app.
errorSelfDemotion: You cannot remove your own admin access. Ask another admin to do it for you.
errorLastAdmin: This is the only admin account left. Promote someone else to admin first, then come back and demote this one.
errorCoworkerNeedsAgent: A coworker must belong to an agent. Nobody has invited this account to an agency yet, and there is no way to assign one from here — the agent adds them from their own Coworkers screen.
errorNotFound: This account no longer exists. Close this and reload the directory.
errorRoleChangeFailed: The role change did not go through.
activityEventsSubAgent: Everything recorded under {{name}}, including their coworkers
auditScopeTitle: Agent and coworker activity only — not a complete audit trail
auditScopeBodyStart: These are business events an agent or one of their coworkers caused: ads created, marked sold or drafted, leads created and moved, and OLX / Instagram crosspost sessions. Sign-ins, admin decisions taken in this control room, and background jobs are
auditScopeBodyEnd: and will never appear below. Events carry no severity either: the colour on each row is this app reading the event type’s outcome, not a level the server stored.
emptyAuditFilteredSub: The log itself may well have activity in it — nothing recorded matches the event type or agent you picked.
emptyAuditSub: Events appear here once an agent or coworker creates an ad, marks one sold, moves a lead, or runs a crosspost session.
subjectDeletedTitle: The ad or lead this event referred to has been deleted
noAgentRecorded: No agent recorded on this event
